requirement: Project charter defines audience, inclusion criteria, object tiers, and exclusions.
evidence: README.md and docs/methods.md define the user, bulk RNA-seq scope, object tiers, admission tests and exclusions.

requirement: No dataset merges without provenance and rights review.
evidence: The collection plan links every biological object to dated intake, rights, reference and transformation records; the overlap audit passes.

requirement: v1 scope remains transcriptomics plus core infrastructure.
evidence: The registry contains bulk RNA-seq objects and two infrastructure fixtures; no other assay is represented.

requirement: Documentation style rules live in CONTRIBUTING.md and are reviewed like code.
evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md states the writing rules; CI checks local links, unfinished text, punctuation and attribution traces.

requirement: Fresh clone can enumerate all datasets from manifests only.
evidence: registry.py discovers manifests without a hand-maintained dataset list; the clean temporary-repository test passes.

requirement: Validator catches duplicate IDs, missing files, invalid hashes, and undeclared roles.
evidence: Regression tests cover duplicate identifiers and roles, missing and changed files, bad hashes and undeclared paths.

requirement: Dataset-specific logic is isolated in adapters/workflows rather than scattered through core code.
evidence: Source retrieval and biological selection live under workflows; src/omicsbench contains source-neutral models, registry, transfer, count and validation code.

requirement: Schema round-trip tests preserve values.
evidence: test_manifest_round_trip passes against the current strict Pydantic contract.

requirement: Provenance report can be generated without reading Python source.
evidence: The provenance command reads the manifest and transformation record and is exercised by the command-line test.

requirement: Help text for fields is written as human guidance, not terse schema jargon.
evidence: Every public manifest field has a plain-language description in the generated JSON Schema.

requirement: Schema changes require tests and migration notes.
evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md requires both; schema drift and manifest round trips are checked automatically.

requirement: Every candidate has an intake record before processing starts.
evidence: The curation intake directory records every evaluated archive candidate, including excluded and deferred sources.

requirement: Rights decision includes evidence and date checked.
evidence: Every biological object carries rights.json and manifest rights fields with the licence, evidence URL, decision and review date.

requirement: Link-only status is visible in catalog and CLI.
evidence: rnaseq-001 is marked original_link in its manifest and command output; retrieval refuses to package it.

requirement: No source is called open simply because a browser download exists.
evidence: GEO records remain AMBER without a specific redistribution grant; downloadable material is not packaged on access alone.

requirement: At least four distinct RNA design archetypes are represented.
evidence: The 12 certified objects declare 12 design descriptions spanning balanced, paired, blocked factorial, imbalanced and stratified comparisons.

requirement: Counts are never overwritten by normalized values.
evidence: Source integer counts and pocket integer counts remain separate; normalization is computed only during validation.

requirement: Strandedness and sample design metadata are explicit.
evidence: Every sample record declares condition, replicate, batch or blocking value and strandedness; unavailable strandedness is stated as unknown.

requirement: Reference/annotation compatibility is checked automatically.
evidence: verify_references.py checks official annotation files and pocket identifiers; certification rejects missing or unresolved evidence.

requirement: All stochastic reducers accept and record a seed.
evidence: Reducers accept a seed and every manifest derivation records it, including zero for deterministic feature selection.

requirement: Paired reads and sample identity are tested.
evidence: Regression tests cover paired-mate identity, duplicate runs, sample order and design-to-matrix agreement.

requirement: Pocket size is justified quantitatively.
evidence: Each object retains its candidate curve and selects the smallest feature count that meets all four predeclared preservation thresholds.

requirement: No spreadsheet-only/manual cleanup is required for regeneration.
evidence: Intake, selection, DESeq2 comparison, reference checking, assembly, catalog and certification are scripted.

requirement: Every dataset has hard and quantitative validation.
evidence: All 12 distributed biological objects and the synthetic fixture have integrity and metric checks. The deliberately link-only rnaseq-001 record carries no redistributed matrix to score.

requirement: Metric definitions include filtering universe and direction.
evidence: Every validation profile states the feature universe, calculation and inclusive minimum for all four metrics.

requirement: Expected outputs rebuild from a pinned baseline.
evidence: All 12 DESeq2 evidence records were rebuilt under R 4.5.3 and DESeq2 1.50.2 with pinned inputs, hashes and one workflow revision.

requirement: Figures are never the only location where expected values exist.
evidence: Exact results and thresholds live in expected JSON, the catalog JSON and catalog TSV; the SVG is generated from those records.

requirement: CLI has unit and end-to-end tests on nano objects.
evidence: All seven public commands are covered by the 45-test suite, including the generated fixture path.

requirement: All downloads verify hashes.
evidence: Transfers verify declared size and SHA-256 before atomic replacement; interrupted and corrupt transfers have regression tests.

requirement: A user can discover, retrieve, inspect, and validate without reading source code.
evidence: The documented command path passes locally. Completion still requires the recorded independent quickstart trial on a fresh checkout.

requirement: Help and error messages are concise and human.
evidence: Every command has focused help and an example; expected user failures return short messages without tracebacks.

requirement: Several datasets regenerate end-to-end from a clean environment.
evidence: The collection rebuilds locally from declared inputs. The pushed candidate still needs a clean hosted run or independent-machine record.

requirement: Resolved parameters and versions are preserved.
evidence: Manifests, transformation records, DESeq2 evidence and runtime/environment-lock.json preserve inputs, parameters, code hashes and software versions.

requirement: No notebook-only hidden step is needed for release artifacts.
evidence: The repository contains scripted workflows for every generated object, catalog, figure, audit and certification output.

requirement: Failures retain logs and a short human summary.
evidence: Rejected pocket and reference candidates retain structured evidence and explanations. A general failure-log contract is not enforced for every workflow.

requirement: Nano CI stays within a defined time budget.
evidence: The workflow has a five-minute limit and the local 45-test suite completes in about 15 seconds. Hosted runtime remains to be confirmed after push.

requirement: Release tag is blocked by schema/hash/registry failures.
evidence: The integrity workflow runs on every push and tag and includes schema drift, manifest hashes, registry validation, overlap audit and preflight.

requirement: Corruption and sample-order failures have regression tests.
evidence: Dedicated corruption, missing-file, duplicate, sample-order and design-mismatch tests pass.

requirement: Documentation quality is reviewed beyond spelling.
evidence: The repository checker covers links and unfinished text; the collection audit detects repeated long prose; the fidelity figure received a rendered layout review.

requirement: Every public command has concise help and one example.
evidence: list, info, get, validate, provenance, verify-cache and doctor each expose an example in command help.

requirement: Every dataset README is usable without opening YAML.
evidence: Each of the 12 biological cards states its design, file contents, commands, measured result, limits, citation and rights location.

requirement: Release notes are manually edited for flow.
evidence: CHANGELOG.md describes the finished v1 collection by user impact, scientific scope and validation evidence.

requirement: No em dash appears in docs/help/release notes.
evidence: The repository checker scans every Markdown file and the current documentation passes.

requirement: Review removes long narration comments.
evidence: A source-wide comment and docstring review found only concise module descriptions and constraint explanations.

requirement: All core figures regenerate from code and source tables.
evidence: scripts/build_catalog.py regenerates figures/v1-fidelity.svg directly from manifests and expected-result records; CI checks drift.

requirement: Captions are concise and units are present where applicable.
evidence: The fidelity figure labels each unitless preservation metric, threshold and object; its README caption states the comparison.

requirement: Rendered documentation is manually inspected.
evidence: The full-resolution fidelity preview has been checked for clipping, collisions, labels and value placement. GitHub and Zenodo rendering remain part of publication verification.

requirement: No visual hides rights or warning status.
evidence: The figure is explicitly scoped to the 12 certified biological objects; the adjacent catalog and README state rights and release status.
